title: Grok Pricing 2026: Every Plan, Rate, and Real Cost
summary: Grok pricing structures determine which features individual users and businesses can access for their specific computational and integration needs.
body_markdown:
## Grok pricing and plans for 2026 explained


Scaling from a[$0/month](https://x.ai/pricing) entry point for casual social media interaction to a **$100 monthly ceiling** for enterprise users, Grok’s 2026 pricing structure matches its cost to the intensity of a user's technical demands.


While the floor is free, the ceiling is dictated by the compute costs of Grok 4.7’s massive context window.


### The Free Tier: Basic access for social users


By offering the Free Tier at[$0/month](https://x.ai/pricing) , xAI is able to use social media interactions as a low-cost RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) pipeline.


When a user operates at this level, they receive limited rate-to-refresh cycles, meaning a standard research session will likely hit a "cool-down" period after just a few complex queries.


This tier is designed for discovery rather than production, as it lacks the dedicated compute priority found in the paid versions.


### Grok Premium: The $20 standard for individuals


**$30/month is the baseline** for individual power users on SuperGrok, compared to the ChatGPT Plus plan which sits at $20/month, forcing consumers to weigh the $10 price difference against superior utility for their investment, as cost becomes a deciding factor alongside feature sets and model performance for the subscriber.


Consumers face an identical financial barrier when choosing between these two competing services.


While the $30 SuperGrok tier represents the standard individual tier, xAI brackets this option with the free tier and the $100 SuperGrok Plus configuration to capture different segments of the consumer market, so users are funneled into specific tiers based on their willingness to pay for varying levels of service.


The free tier provides basic access for casual users, whereas the $30 SuperGrok tier introduces priority queue access for heavier individual workloads, meaning that speed and responsiveness are gated behind a higher monthly commitment.


However, these low-cost entry points merely serve as a prelude to the true operational costs found in the Pro and Enterprise tiers. When users transition to high-frequency API usage and massive context windows, the monthly spend rapidly escalates toward the $300 ceiling.


This subscription unlocks Grok 4.7 for sustained use, though it still operates under shared hardware resources. For users who need to bridge these capabilities into automated workflows,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) bills one credit per flow run regardless of the number of steps inside it.


By decoupling the cost from the granularity of the logic, it ensures that breaking a complex Grok prompt into a reliable multi-step chain does not increase the platform fee.


### Grok Pro and Enterprise: Scaling to $300 monthly


Professional and Enterprise tiers scale costs based on context window utilization, where the true expense of long-horizon reasoning becomes visible. The following figures show how remaining token capacity diminishes as initial prompt size increases within the 1M context window:


A token represents the basic unit of data processed by the model, roughly equivalent to four characters of text or a single syllable in a word.


The context window defines the total number of these tokens that Grok can hold in its active memory during a single interaction.


When a user submits a massive prompt, the model must process and remember every single token simultaneously, which requires immense computational power and drives up the operational cost.


- After a 200k prompt,[800,000 tokens](https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing) remain available, providing enough room for deep analysis of several large technical manuals.
- After a 500k prompt, 500,000 tokens remain, effectively halving the model's "memory" for the rest of the conversation.
- After an 800k prompt, only 200,000 tokens remain, forcing the user to either truncate their data or pay for a context refresh.


Because xAI must reserve significant VRAM to maintain state across such large datasets, these high-density prompts drive the monthly spend toward $300. Consequently, an enterprise running multiple 800k-token agents will find their "unlimited" access quickly gated by these tiered pricing increments.
